title: Microsoft Rebuilds Copilot Around Agents and Usage Billing
summary: Microsoft’s redesigned Copilot combines Office, coding, and an always-on Autopilot agent while shifting enterprise AI toward metered consumption.
body:
Microsoft is repositioning Copilot as a broader work platform, combining familiar chat functions with software creation and persistent task execution. The redesigned app is organized around three areas: Home, which brings together conversations and Microsoft 365 context; Code, which extends GitHub Copilot-style development tools to a wider group of knowledge workers; and Autopilot, a proactive agent intended to continue working after the user leaves.

The change is more than a visual refresh. Microsoft is trying to make Copilot the front door to work across documents, applications, data, and software projects. Code lowers the boundary between asking for an answer and asking for a working application, while Autopilot represents a move from request-response assistance toward delegated workflows.

Microsoft is also changing how customers may pay for that work. New Microsoft 365 Copilot Business licenses purchased through its channel will move toward usage-based billing by default from November 2. Consumption is measured through Copilot Credits, allowing Microsoft to charge according to the volume and complexity of AI activity rather than treating every user as an identical subscription seat.

That model could make low-intensity usage cheaper, but it also introduces budgeting and governance problems for companies whose agents run continuously or touch large amounts of enterprise data. Administrators will need to understand not only who has access, but which workflows generate the most consumption and whether the resulting work is valuable.

The strategic importance is clear: Microsoft is tying the agent transition to both its productivity suite and its revenue model. If Autopilot becomes a routine layer over Office, software development, and business data, Copilot could become an operating surface for knowledge work. If metered costs arrive before reliability and controls, enterprises may treat the new autonomy as a financial liability rather than a productivity upgrade.
title_zh: 微软重构Copilot：办公、编程与自动代理合一
summary_zh: 微软将Office、编程和持续运行的Autopilot智能体纳入新版Copilot，并推动企业AI转向按实际使用量计费。
body_zh:
微软正在把Copilot重新定位为更完整的工作平台，把传统聊天功能与软件创建和持续执行任务的能力合并起来。新版应用主要分为三个区域：Home负责汇集对话和Microsoft 365上下文；Code把类似GitHub Copilot的开发能力扩展到更多知识工作者；Autopilot则是一个可以在用户离开后继续执行任务的主动式智能体。

这不只是界面更新。微软试图让Copilot成为连接文档、应用、数据和软件项目的工作入口。Code缩短了“提出问题”与“生成可运行应用”之间的距离，Autopilot则把产品从问答式助手推向任务委托式工作流。

微软同时改变了收费方式。自11月2日起，通过渠道购买的新Microsoft 365 Copilot Business许可证将默认采用按量计费。用量以Copilot Credits计算，微软可以根据AI活动的数量和复杂程度收费，而不再把所有用户视为相同的订阅席位。

这种方式可能让低频用户付费更低，但也会带来预算和治理难题。企业需要掌握的不只是“谁能使用”，还包括哪些智能体工作流消耗最多额度，以及这些消耗是否真正产生了价值。

这项更新的战略意义在于，微软正把智能体转型同时绑定到生产力套件和收入模型上。如果Autopilot成为覆盖Office、软件开发和企业数据的日常工作层，Copilot就可能成为知识工作的操作入口；但如果计量收费先于可靠性和控制能力成熟，企业也可能把这种自主性视为成本风险。

cat_take_zh: Copilot真正的分水岭不是功能数量，而是企业能否管住Autopilot的持续消耗
cat_take_en: Copilot’s decisive test is whether enterprises can control Autopilot’s ongoing consumption, not whether Microsoft adds more features.
